source.title: Diffused Redundancy in Pre-trained Representations
source.authors: Vedant Nanda; Till Speicher; John P. Dickerson; S. Feizi; Krishna P. Gummadi; Adrian Weller

record.tranche_reason: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and discusses polysemanticity as background, but its experiments measure diffuse redundancy in pretrained vision representations, not superposition, feature sparsity, feature directions, or SAE features.
record.gate_note: The paper reports measurements of random-neuron-subset redundancy, a related but different construct. These results do not establish whether features are stored as overlapping directions or whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity. It also compares random projections and PCA subsets, but those results do not measure any of the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition and polysemanticity only as background. Its experiments measure diffused redundancy: how well random subsets of penultimate-layer neurons in ImageNet-pretrained vision models match the full layer on linear probes and CKA. It does not measure feature directions, overlap or superposition geometry, sparsity transitions, capacity allocation, the causes of polysemanticity, LLM features, SAE features or feature dimensionality. The layer-width result (Fig 6) is about redundancy fading in narrow layers, not about features sharing dimensions, so it is a related but different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also report that random subsets of size k track the top-k principal components and beat random projections. They say redundancy appears only in sufficiently wide layers and persists under MRL, dropout and DeCov. They caution that dropping neurons concentrates accuracy loss on a few classes, a possible fairness-efficiency tradeoff.
record.recipe_differences: The study measures random subsets of pretrained vision-model neurons using downstream linear probes and CKA; it does not use the toy sparse-feature setup or measure superposition geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported redundancy varies with pretraining loss and dataset, downstream dataset, and representation width.

fits_no_version.finding: Random subsets of penultimate-layer neurons in ImageNet-pretrained vision models keep most of the full layer's linear-probe accuracy. Table 1 DR values at δ=0.9 range from 0.20 to 0.95, depending on model and downstream task. The redundancy shrinks as the layer is narrowed (ResNet50 ff8 needs over 90% of its neurons), is larger with adversarial training and ImageNet21k pretraining, and is barely affected by dropout or DeCov.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained vision representations show diffused redundancy: sufficiently large random neuron subsets match full-layer downstream performance, and this emerges only when layers are wide enough.

record.problems: The paper's measurements address diffuse neuron-subset redundancy in vision models, not the claim's feature-superposition mechanism. Table 1 gives no uncertainty for its reported values; the paper describes error bars from random subset selections elsewhere.
record.rows_left_out: No Table 1 results were left out. Other figures and appendices also report diffuse-redundancy curves and qualitative comparisons, but those results are not claim-version tests and are omitted to keep the record focused on the table's explicitly tabulated model-by-task measurements.

untested.parts: No toy sparse-feature models; no overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transition or regular geometry measured.
No test of feature importance or capacity deciding dedicated versus shared dimensions. The width experiment (Fig 6) measures redundancy, not polysemanticity.
No measurement of polysemantic neurons or their causes.
Vision models only; no LLMs and no dictionary or SAE recovery. Random-subset probe accuracy is not a measure of features spread across neurons in the claim's sense.

record.verdict_notes: Rows are correctly linked to none. Table 1 values check out against the text. The states are cannot_determine because none of the rows measure a claim version. The narrowing-width result is suggestive of capacity effects, but it measures redundancy rather than superposition or polysemanticity, so it is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a V2 test.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test feature superposition, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular feature geometry in toy networks.
The study does not test whether feature importance or limited capacity makes some features dedicated and others shared.
The study does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity indicates superposition.
The experiments are on vision models and do not measure feature spread across neurons in LLMs or recover sparse features with a dictionary.
The study does not evaluate whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
The study does not measure the dimensionality or geometry of individual features.

relation.reason: Toy Models of Superposition and polysemanticity appear as background citations; the experimental methods neither test nor use superposition.

tranche.reason: The experiments measure redundant downstream information in random subsets of vision-model neurons, a related construct that does not establish overlapping feature directions, capacity-driven polysemanticity, or any other listed claim version.

source_check.notes: The DR threshold concerns average relative performance over sampled neuron subsets, not a guarantee for every subset. No statements or verdicts were listed in this check pack.
